subject: biology

items.q: Where does most of a plant's mass come from?
items.correct: From carbon dioxide in the air, via photosynthesis.
items.misconception: From minerals taken up from the soil.
items.random_wrong: From the water it drinks only.
items.why: Photosynthesis fixes CO₂ into glucose, which builds the plant's structures — soil supplies only small amounts of minerals.

items.correct: All the time, day and night.
items.misconception: Only at night, when they can't photosynthesise.
items.why: Plants respire continuously to release energy; they additionally photosynthesise when there is light.

items.correct: No — it stores light energy as chemical energy in glucose.
items.misconception: Yes, plants create new energy from nothing.
items.why: Energy can't be created; photosynthesis transfers light energy into chemical energy in glucose.

items.q: Where in the cell does photosynthesis happen?
items.correct: In the chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll.
items.why: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs light energy for photosynthesis; mitochondria are for respiration.
